fix: Keep the snapshot but reuse a retained buffer, as update_compositor already does with compositor_scratch: add a field such as `nested_jobs: Vec<NestedJob>` to the input state, then in route_nested_remainder do `let mut jobs = std::mem::take(&mut self.input.nested_jobs); jobs.clear(); jobs.extend(bracket.outer.iter().filter(|link| link.axis == bracket.axis).map(|link| Job { ... }));` (move the Job struct to module scope so the field can name it), iterate `for job in jobs.drain(..)`, and restore with `self.input.nested_jobs = jobs;` before returning. Remove the `if jobs.is_empty()` check, since an empty drain is a no-op. Note the early `return`s inside the loop must also restore the buffer, or the scratch is simply rebuilt on the next event.

fix: Filter in place instead of collecting a second Vec on every pointer move: `let mut path = self.hit_test(position.hit_point).and_then(|render| self.element_for_render(render)).map(|element| self.drag_target_ancestors(element)).unwrap_or_default();` (before the get_mut), then after `let source_context = active.source.context_id();` call `path.retain(|(_, target)| target.context_id() == source_context);`. The per-move allocation in drag_target_ancestors (Vec::new then push at line 2220) is the other per-event Vec; it can be written into a retained scratch buffer if it shows up in a profile.

Collect into a retained buffer, not a new Vec on every busy frame: add a tree field (like compositor_scratch in tree.rs:1349) typed as the same 7-tuple, then `let mut tickers = std::mem::take(&mut self.ticker_scratch); tickers.clear(); tickers.extend(self.tracked.compositor_nodes.iter().filter_map(...));` drop the redundant `let mut tickers = tickers;` rebinding, iterate `for (...) in tickers.drain(..)`, and store `self.ticker_scratch = tickers;` after the loop.

Same pattern as tick_controllers: use a retained scratch buffer field (e.g. `viewport_scratch: Vec<(RenderObjectId, ElementId, ScrollDelegate)>`), `take` it, `clear` and `extend` it, iterate with `drain(..)` while calling self.mark_render_dirty, then put it back. The collect runs on every busy frame that contains an animating sliver viewport, so the allocation repeats for the whole animation. The Rc clone of config.delegate is intended and stays.

        tickers.sort_by_key(|(render, ..)| render.0);
fix: `tickers.sort_unstable_by_key(|(render, ..)| render.0);` Render ids are unique, so the stable merge buffer is unnecessary. This matches the `sort_unstable_by_key` already used in update_compositor (line 2797).

Drain instead of taking the Vec, so its capacity is kept for the next `active.entered.push` at line 2278: `active.target = None; for (_, target) in active.entered.drain(..) { target.leave(); }`. `active` is an exclusive borrow of self.input, so the leave callbacks cannot re-enter the tree and the drain is safe. Only target changes reach this path, so the cost is low.

The compositor visit list is taken from `compositor_scratch` at line 2783 and only put back at line 2314 (end of the function). When the `?` at this line returns early, the buffer is dropped and is empty on the next frame, so it reallocates. Restore it before propagating, for example by moving the loop body into a helper or by matching the result: `if let Err(error) = self.layout_render(_render, constraints) { self.compositor_scratch = nodes; return Err(error); }`. This only affects the error path.
